candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Because RFP timelines tend to compress at the end, I expect the turnaround for this work to be last-minute, although I suspect the RFP itself will be released next quarter. Nadia, I’m seeking layout and design support for the resulting response (proposal), which will need to follow strict rules for file size, page numbers, and similar details. 1) Have you supported this type of proposal before? 2) If so, how do you prepare with clients for these timelines, particularly when client edits may continue until the proposal is final?

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Thank you, Nadia—the same to you! After reviewing the current proposal, I found that the full document totals 126 pages, including all letters, forms, and other materials. Of those 126 pages, 74 pages have a graphic touch. Could you provide an approximate budget range for supporting the project? Please include one budget with 3 simple infographics and 2 simple maps, plus a separate budget without those items. Thank you!

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: While the RFP is still awaiting publication, the team is preparing everything in advance. Good morning, Nadia—RCP, the engineering firm, wants to move forward with you, and they will ask you to sign an NDA as part of that process. Once it is completed, I can send over the previous proposal and supporting documents so you can begin working on the layout, branding, resumes, and related materials. Thanks!

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Because we can reuse the template from our last submission, maps, infographics, and similar elements may not be necessary. That could mean fewer work hours and a total below $7800—excellent!

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Hi Nadia! Separate from the Rcp project, I’m planning a response to an RFQ, and the work should be pretty straightforward. The scope covers packaging all content into one doc., along with layout, the org. chart, the budget sheet, and formatting. Although the response is due 9/16, I plan to submit it on 9/15. Would you be interested in helping me with this task? If so, could you provide the total cost? I’ll also send the RFQ shortly for reference. Thanks!

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Because this is an RFQ rather than an RFP, I suspect the response can be slightly shorter—perhaps capped at 34 pages. That feels about right.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text:
Unfortunately, the earlier proposal is beyond my budget and includes more scope than I need. Could the simpler version instead focus on a single formatting/layout pass over the final draft, using Civic Canopy's existing brand colors and fonts, followed by one round of revisions and delivery as a print-ready PDF?

More specifically, what I need is 1) layout and graphic treatment for the complete document and 2) application of the tables, photos, org chart, and graphics to the final draft.

Because the RFQ is usually the first step, I suspect there is also a chance that an RFP will follow later. What would this reduced version cost?

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text:
The estimate you sent, $3100.00, works for me. Thank you.

A few follow-up items:

1) Would a 72-hour turnaround for the draft after I provide the final narrative, followed by a 72-hour turnaround on your end for final revisions, be workable? My subcontractors will not send their content until EOD next Friday, so your working window will be compressed.

2) I have shifted the branding from the client to the bidder—me—so please design it around my company's identity, Blue Mesa Strategies. I can provide the logo and colors.

3) This will be the first proposal I submit as a prime (I launched my company less than a year ago, and I’m solo), so I want it to serve as a reusable template and not have to rebuild future proposals from scratch. Please make the sections swappable and modular: a) a flexible narrative structure (for example, 12 sections vs. 18 sections), b) a modular table style that resizes for different budget structures, and c) a “prepared for ___ [client name]” credit line rather than client branding.

4) Canva: Will I still own the files if I do not have a paid subscription? Will source files exist in another format, or will everything be entirely in Canva?

Thank you!

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: 3) For now, then, let's keep the first proposal simple and leave revisiting the template for the future. One thing I still need confirmed: after your final review, can I make any necessary last-minute edits in Canva?

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Hi! Thanks, and I'm going to attach the skeleton now. Two notes to keep in mind - 1) the section order is fixed by the client's Q&A (which came out Tuesday morning) and cannot be redesigned , so we need to stick to the order in this skeleton, and 2) the final deliverable is one PDF submitted by email, so the template should be built for clean PDF export that is "emailable" (not sure if I mentioned this before). Thank you!

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: 1) For the document, please use photos from this folder: <https://drive.blue-mesa.example/folders/HarborWorkspaceFolderDemo0064?usp=sharing>. The ones that definitely need to appear are those with asterisks in their titles.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: 2) When the final file is saved, it is critical that all the proposal’s many hyperlinks continue to function. I’m noting this now to make sure they still work at that stage. Thanks!

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: 3) Within each appropriate section, please keep the font type consistent and use a consistent, appropriate font size.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Hi! A contractor has just sent me 11 resumes for the proposal, and I wasn’t expecting the additional team members. As a result, I need to create 11 more bios for the Appendix under Signal Grove Studio. Could you add placeholders for these 11 bios so I can drop them in during my review? Thanks.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Nadia—I’m sorry, but I need five tables in the proposal replaced. The revised five tables are available in this doc: <https://docs.blue-mesa.example/document/d/CedarBudgetNotesDemo0087/edit?usp=sharing>. I’m hoping you haven’t reached that part of the layout yet; if you have, I hope replacing them won’t be too much of an inconvenience. Thank you.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: In case you can insert them directly instead of using the placeholders, I’ve just added the new bios to the Tables doc as well. Thank you!!

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text:
Thanks—this approach works for me.

I hadn’t anticipated the document becoming this long, so I’m hoping we can tighten the spacing between paragraphs and sections to bring it closer to the original page limit. When I reach the review, I’d also like to condense the letter \(first page\) to one page.

If anything else feels awkward, I can try cutting the content further during my review if doing so would help. I appreciate you collaborating with me and continuing to share progress updates.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: 1) Could we try a different background treatment for the cover, TOC, Page Divider for Appendix, and Last Page? I’m not fond of the light pink/cream wash on those pages. If another concept doesn’t come to mind, my fallback preference is white so they match the remainder of the document.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: 2) The letter is going to be one page, and I need to add my signature. I’m hoping the signature will be easy to insert in Canva. Please note that the two pics currently on the second page of the letter are two of my favorites in the proposal, so if they cannot fit in the one-page letter, could you move them to another section?

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: 3) Could you adjust the image on Page 32 so the tree stands out more, perhaps by using a wider zoom?

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: 4) On Page 42, please remove the photograph of the boy wearing a white t-shirt in front of the garden. You can either substitute another photo or leave one pic on that page.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: 5) In the photo with the lady on Page 47, could the framing be adjusted to reveal more of the tree?

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: 6) Could you also reframe the photo on Page 74 so the full tree is visible?

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Nadia—unfortunately, the Payment and Milestone Schedule table now needs five rows per phase. I placed the revised table in the Google doc that was shared yesterday. I’m unsure whether it will be easier to insert five rows per phase into the existing layout or replace the entire table, so please use whichever approach works best. When you reach this revision, let me know if you have any questions. Thanks.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: While reviewing between meetings, I noticed one item, Nadia, and will post any further issues here as I find them. 1) The crop on page 23 has lost the intended view of the tree. Could you zoom out slightly so a little more of the tree becomes visible again? Thanks.
